title: Introduce quiet-checkpoint CI schedulers and presubmit warm cache
author: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Summary: This PR refactors the presubmit orchestration layer to introduce 'quiet checkpoints' in the CI scheduler and a lightweight presubmit cache warm path. Motivation: our team has observed frequent noisy reruns from transient infra flakiness and duplicate lint/test runs for the same logical change. Quiet checkpoints reduce churn by deferring nonblocking checks and collapsing equivalent presubmit executions; the presubmit warm cache reduces cold-start time for heavy integration shards by reusing cached build artifacts across ephemeral runners.

Scope:
- Split scheduler responsibilities between fast-feedback lanes (lint/unit smoke) and quiet lanes (expensive integration + optional flakiness probes).
- Add a per-PR checkpointing state machine (in-memory + persistent marker in /tmp/ci-checkpoints) so reruns within a short window are deduplicated.
- Implement presubmit cache warm: a gated step that attempts to fetch and restore a minimal build cache before heavy test shards run; if fetch fails we fall back to normal flow.
- Normalize exit codes and CI annotations for flaky vs failed checks so the bot can auto-retry only deterministic failures.
- Add dependency gate for routine dep-updates: a lightweight verifier runs after dep bump PRs to assert lockfile hygiene and run a focused subset of integration tests.

Checklist:
- [x] Scheduler split implemented and unit-tested locally
- [x] Deduplication marker + TTL implemented
- [x] Presubmit cache warm implemented with safe fallback
- [x] Lints updated and adjusted for new job ordering
- [x] CI matrices updated and smoke pipeline added
- [x] Deployment plan written and canary toggles added in console (feature:ci_quiet_checkpoint)

Testing & rollout:
- Local CI runner: ran subsets of lint and unit shards with cached warm path.
- Staging: enrolled 20% of main PRs behind the feature flag for 48h; observed 18% reduction in duplicate job starts and 12% median reduction in presubmit end-to-end time for infra-heavy PRs.
- Canaries: one-week canary validated no regressions in critical paths and no increase in test flakiness rates.

Backwards compatibility: The default behavior without the feature flag is unchanged; the quiet checkpoint TTL defaults to 5 minutes and is adjustable via /ci/configs/checkpoint.yaml.

Related: ENG-2051 (CI throughput improvements), ENG-2099 (presubmit cache RFC).

Links: design doc: https://linear.app/redwood/issue/ENG-2051/ci-quiet-checkpoints design diagram: https://company-internal/redwood/diagrams/ci-quiet-checkpoint.svg

Rollout plan in PR body above.

Rationale: This change is intended to reduce build spend on duplicate work and improve developer signal by keeping noisy nonblocking checks out of the fast-feedback lane. It also reduces cold-start latency for heavy shards which disproportionately affect PR turnaround for runtime and model-registry changes.

release_notes:
- Introduced CI quiet checkpoints to reduce duplicate presubmit runs.
- Added presubmit cache warm step to reduce cold-start latency for heavy test shards.
- Split presubmit scheduler into fast-feedback and quiet lanes; normalization of CI annotations and exit codes.
- Feature-gated rollout: ci_quiet_checkpoint (off by default).
